question: SIAE Microelettronica SpA is an Italian company that is currently participating in the Important Project of Common European Interest on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (IPCEI ME/CT). To support the implementation of IPCEI ME/CT, Italy allocated additional resources through its National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) by means of milestone M4C2-I2.1.
As a result, SIAE Microelettronica SpA’s project will receive funding worth EUR 179.22 million, of which EUR 63.05 million from Italy’s NRRP1.

Despite benefiting from massive public and private funding, many jobs at SIAE Microelettronica SpA – a company that is considered to be of strategic importance to its sector because of its work in the fields of research, development and innovation – are at risk, an alarming development.

SIAE Microelettronica SpA’s highly skilled and specialised workforce is an important asset for both Italy's and Europe's competitiveness. Employees, trade unions, politicians and institutional representatives are taking action to prevent any redundancies and collective dismissals at SIAE, as well as to ward off the risk of relocation. In the light of the above: 1.
Could the proper and prompt use of the aforementioned PNRR funds save the jobs in question and, if so, how?

What actions could be taken to protect the industrial production of key technologies in the EU and to strengthen its global competitiveness during the green and digital transition while safeguarding high-quality jobs and opposing any plans to relocate production sites?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.4.2025) Italy’s Recovery and Resilience Plan provides for the financing for a total of EUR 1.5 billion of the so-called ‘IPCEI Fund’, which is also financed through national resources.

The objective of the measure is to provide support through the Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEI) Fund to projects belonging to four IPCEIs, namely, (i) the ‘Microelectronics and Communication Technologies’ IPCEI, (ii) the ‘Hydrogen Technology value chain’ IPCEI, (iii) the ‘Hydrogen related infrastructure and applications in the industrial sector’ IPCEI and (iv) the ‘Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services’ IPCEI.

The Commission notes that innovative projects are generally expected to result in the creation of highly skilled jobs by the enterprises that undertake them. The Commission is committed to strengthening the global competitiveness of the EU industry and net-zero technologies supply chains.

Such initiatives aim to provide predictability, certainty and long-term signals to incentivise demand and create conditions that facilitate investments in net-zero technology manufacturing, while supporting the workforce needed in this sector. This work will draw on the report by Mario Draghi with the goal to enable sustainable prosperity and competitiveness.

As its first major initiative, the Commission has presented a Competitiveness Compass that will frame the work for the rest of the term. The Commission has also launched a Clean Industrial Deal and proposes a Circular Economy Act, a European Competitiveness Fund, as well as risk-absorbing measures to promote private investments in innovation and the twin transition.
The Commission will aim to ensure that these efforts benefit all, including by supporting quality jobs.
